label: Bhadawari

names.text: "Bhadwari" and "Etawah" from the Wikipedia article's other-names line. "Badavan" and "Etawah" from the Wikipedia list's alternate-name field. "Bhadawan" is the spelling Zachariah (1941) used, per the Buffalopedia page, and is left out of the list. "Badavan" appears on the list page only.

about.text: A river buffalo of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh in India, kept mainly in Agra and Etawah in Uttar Pradesh and in Bhind and Morena in Madhya Pradesh. It is kept for milk, with butterfat recorded as high, and for draught work. The pure breed has dwindled to a few thousand animals through crossbreeding with the Murrah.

sources.text: Wikipedia article: distribution (Agra, Etawah, Bhind, Morena), dairy and draught use, the "only several thousand" pure animals and the Murrah crossing. Buffalopedia page: the tract of Agra, Etawah, Jalaun, Auraiya, Jhansi and Lalitpur in Uttar Pradesh and Bhind and Morena in Madhya Pradesh, and the fat range. The list page gives use as dairy and draught. Protein is not mentioned in the text.

origin.place: Bhadawar estate, in Bah tehsil of Agra District, Uttar Pradesh, and nearby areas of the former Gwalior State. Found in the ravines of the Yamuna and Chambal rivers.

sources.text: Buffalopedia page: the breed takes its name from the Bhadawar estate (Kaura, 1961); Zachariah (1941) first described it. Breeding tract and ravine location from the same page, citing Kushwaha et al. (2007). The Wikipedia article gives Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh as origin. No formation dates were found.

Buffalopedia page, citing Kushwaha et al. (2007): estimated population in the breeding tract was 30,000. The page also gives 1,139 thousand in Uttar Pradesh in 1977 and 982 thousand in 1991, and a 2007 breed-wise census of 724 thousand; the census figure conflicts with the survey estimates and is not used.

Buffalopedia trait table, IGFRI herd at Jhansi: lactation milk yield 1,231.93 kg (n = 188), lactation length 291.46 days. Wikipedia: lactation of 272 days with average yield 752 to 810 kg in that period. The min is from Wikipedia and the max from the IGFRI herd. These are two different sources and conditions, not one range.

Buffalopedia page: fat range 5.5 to 14%, and the IGFRI herd average 8.09%. Wikipedia gives butterfat 6.0 to as high as 12.5%, with no source inline. The range is the Buffalopedia figure. Protein is not given; the page gives solids-not-fat at 10.90%, which is not used here.
The list page gives use as "dairy, draught" and calls it a selectively improved river type. The Wikipedia article describes its use as dairy.

facts.v: Two white lines on the lower neck, a distinguishing feature.

gaps: No FAO DAD-IS risk status found; the Wikipedia and Buffalopedia pages both give none, and the Buffalopedia page gives no formal conservation category. No formation dates. The population figures disagree: the 2007 breed-wise census gives 724 thousand, the tract survey 30,000, and the Wikipedia article says only several thousand pure animals remain. The 2007 survey figure is used, but the current size is unknown. No protein figure. No per-year yield found. Lactation range mixes two sources. "Palitana" and "Bhadawan" as separate names were not used.
